'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*The [[Government of Chad|Chadian government]] announces that an overnight attack on [[Chad]]'s security services headquarters in [[N'Djamena]] has resulted in the deaths of several individuals, and accuses the [[Socialist Party without Borders]] of carrying out the attack. In response the [[Chadian Army]] besieges the party's headquarters with several people killed including its president [[Yaya Dillo Djérou]] amid internet restrictions around the capital. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-68424115 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/2/28/chad-announces-several-deaths-after-foiled-intelligence-office-attack (Al Jazeera English)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2024/02/29/chad-opposition-leader-yaya-dillo-killed/84bc875c-d718-11ee-82ad-c2391b06a8f5_story.html (The Washington Post)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Petroleum|Oil]] begins to [[Oil spill|wash ashore]] on [[Bonaire]], [[Leeward Antilles]], believed to have originated from the ship {{MV|Gulfstream||2}} with around 35,000 barrels of oil on board that capsized near [[Tobago]] earlier this month. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-68413102.amp?fbclid=IwAR2F9FvKU7sEzgMEd_3m23kzBy6otAcQOKHStvESq0aq_8v0ErTIc2WKjjY (BBC News)]
*At least 17 people are killed after two buses collide in [[San Juan de Opoa]], [[Copán Department]], [[Honduras]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bus-crash-leaves-least-17-dead-honduras-2024-02-28/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–NATO relations]]
**[[Russia]] announces that it will take retaliatory "military-technical" steps in response to [[Sweden]] [[enlargement of NATO|joining]] [[NATO]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2024/02/28/Russia-says-it-will-take-military-technical-steps-in-response-to-Sweden-joining-NATO (Al Arabiya)]
*[[China]] urges the world's largest [[nuclear state]]s to negotiate a "[[no first use]]" treaty. China and [[India]] are currently the only two nuclear powers to formally maintain a no first use policy. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china-urges-un-define-roadmap-exempt-non-nuclear-states-nuclear-threat-state-2024-02-28/ (Reuters)]
*Officials in the Russia-backed breakaway region of [[Transnistria]], internationally recognised as a part of [[Moldova]], appeal to the [[Russian Duma]] for more intervention in Transnistria amid increasing tension with the government of Moldova. [https://apnews.com/article/moldova-transnistria-russia-customs-tiraspol-moscow-duma-fa123a45912a2018f7aec573dde05033 (Associated Press)]
*The [[Canada|Canadian]] [[Government of Canada|government]] releases its report into the high-profile firings of two scientists from the [[National Microbiology Laboratory]] in [[Winnipeg]], [[Manitoba]], in 2021, stating that the pair worked closely and covertly with the [[China|Chinese]] [[Government of China|government]]. [https://nationalpost.com/news/canada/fired-winnipeg-scientists-worked-with-chinese-csis/wcm/7570ac03-fe7c-4895-ae4a-9b99a3d93024/amp/?fbclid=IwAR3OCUpoAijm8ftMZGA9gTlLQNH80CY6y9OoRh1SThqCnA1YmEgW_jsUUnE (''National Post'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Federal prosecution of Donald Trump (election obstruction case)|Federal prosecution of Donald Trump]]
**The [[United States]] [[United States Supreme Court|Supreme Court]] agrees to decide whether former [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] can claim immunity in [[special counsel]] [[Jack Smith (lawyer)|Jack Smith]]'s [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 presidential election]] subversion case. Arguments are scheduled to begin in April. [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/02/28/us/supreme-court-trump-immunity-trial.html?fbclid=IwAR1q0-vM2cEAg-chziJ5M4eWVAR65bHVFjj_VWcYv1ZWY9q3tAEW8Ya-NrA (''The New York Times'')]
*[[LGBT rights in Ghana]]
**The [[Parliament of Ghana]] passes [[Ghanaian anti-LGBT bill|a bill]] making the promotion or advocacy of LGBT rights punishable by five years in prison. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ghanas-parliament-passes-anti-lgbt-law-2024-02-28/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Megxit]]
**In the [[United Kingdom]], [[High Court of Justice]] Judge [[Peter Richard Lane]] rejects a legal challenge from [[Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex|Prince Harry]] against the government's decision to take away the prince's automatic right to police protection when he is in the country. [https://news.sky.com/story/harry-loses-legal-challenge-against-decision-to-take-away-his-police-protection-13082689?fbclid=IwAR0EuTW9dDBvg2r4GqI2KEc0lxYiPmfQ8MVkv1Sp12z4msDkT04isiHRfJE (Sky News)]
*[[U.S. Senator]] [[Mitch McConnell]] announces that he will step down as [[Senate minority leader]] in November, having served as the [[Senate Republican Conference|Senate GOP]] leader since [[110th United States Congress#Leadership|2007]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/mcconnell-step-senate-gop-leader-after-decade-helm/story?id=107639225 (ABC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Red Bull Racing|Red Bull]] [[Formula One]] leader [[Christian Horner]] is cleared of wrongdoing in an internal probe looking into allegations of "inappropriate" behavior made by a female staffer. Horner will remain in the position of team leader. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/sports/red-bull-clears-christian-horner-investigation-formula-1-team-boss-rcna140670 (NBC News)]
